framework: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1755 (arrangements under Reg. (EU) 2024/1689 Arts 92(6), 101(6))
requirement_paraphrase: When the Commission decides to request access to a GPAI model for an Art. 92 evaluation, the decision sets technical means, conditions and a time limit; access may include APIs, internal access, source code, model weights, hosting infrastructure and the ability to inspect and modify system state; providers must not impose constraints that materially impede the evaluation, may be required to disable logging of the Commission's access, and must grant access without undue delay and within the time limit.
what_is_tested: Regulator-run evaluation of GPAI models (access conditions)
who_tests: Commission / AI Office; appointed independent experts
interpretation_note: Binding on GPAI providers once the Commission adopts an access decision; failing to give access is fineable under AI Act Art 101(1)(d). Adopted 20 July 2026, OJ 21.7.2026, in force on the twentieth day after publication.

framework: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1755 (arrangements under Reg. (EU) 2024/1689 Arts 92(6), 101(6))
requirement_paraphrase: Independent experts evaluating GPAI models for the Commission must be independent of providers (shared ownership, governance, staff or resources and contracts with the provider over at least the prior 12 months are considered), declare interests, and keep confidentiality and information-security protocols; providers may submit reasoned observations on appointed experts; experts are selected by call for expressions of interest (standing list possible), directly from the scientific panel, or under the Financial Regulation.
what_is_tested: Independence and selection of external evaluators of GPAI models
interpretation_note: Binding on the Commission and appointed experts. Art 3(6)(c) cross-refers to 'paragraph 4' though provider observations are in paragraph 5 (apparent drafting slip).

framework: EU AI Act - Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content (Section 1, providers)
requirement_paraphrase: Before placing a generative AI system on the market or putting it into service, and regularly thereafter, signatories test their marking and detection solutions against the Code's requirements under conditions representative of real-world use, using internal benchmarks and industry best practice until recognised methods emerge; they may involve independent experts (notably red teaming for adversarial robustness) or test in AI regulatory sandboxes, and follow up shortcomings.
what_is_tested: Pre-market and periodic testing of AI-content marking and detection
interpretation_note: Code is voluntary, but the Commission (8 July 2026) and AI Board (9 July 2026) assessed it as adequate to facilitate compliance with binding Art 50(2) and (5), which apply from 2 August 2026; signing is a route to demonstrate compliance. Final code published 10 June 2026.

framework: EU AI Act - Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content (Section 1, providers)
requirement_paraphrase: Signatories measure detection accuracy (e.g. error rates) on varied samples, including other systems' content and data not used in training, across content length, size, diversity and semantics; they also test robustness to common processing operations (compression, cropping, paraphrasing, translation, print-and-scan) and to adversarial attacks (copying, removal, regeneration, modification of marks) using the same metrics; compliance is demonstrated before market placement and over the lifecycle.
what_is_tested: Reliability and robustness metrics for watermark/marking detection
interpretation_note: Operationalises Art 50(2) second sentence (effective, interoperable, robust, reliable). Robustness measure does not apply to systems exceptionally using only one metadata marking layer (Measure 1.1). Voluntary code assessed adequate (July 2026).

framework: EU AI Act - GPAI Code of Practice (Safety and Security chapter)
requirement_paraphrase: To support post-market monitoring, signatories give an adequate number of independent external evaluators free access to the most capable model version on the market, its chains-of-thought if available, and the least-mitigated corresponding version (unless the model is similarly safe or safer), publish selection criteria, do not train on evaluators' test inputs/outputs without permission, and take no legal or technical retaliation against evaluators who test and publish findings within stated limits.
what_is_tested: Third-party post-market evaluation access and safe harbour
interpretation_note: Code voluntary; Commission Opinion C(2025) 5361 found the S&S chapter adequately covers Art 55(1), so adherence is a route to demonstrate compliance with binding systemic-risk obligations. Distinct from EU-GPAI-CoP-009, which covers monitoring methods.

framework: EU AI Act - GPAI Code of Practice (Safety and Security chapter)
requirement_paraphrase: Signatories report serious incidents involving their model to the AI Office (and national authorities as applicable) in an initial report within 2 days for serious irreversible critical-infrastructure disruption, 5 days for serious cybersecurity breaches incl. weight exfiltration, 10 days for a death and 15 days for serious health, fundamental-rights, property or environmental harm; intermediate reports at least every four weeks; a final report with root cause analysis within 60 days of resolution; records kept five years.
what_is_tested: Serious incident tracking and reporting for systemic-risk models
interpretation_note: Operationalises AI Act Art 55(1)(c) (binding, without fixed deadlines in the Act). Voluntary code assessed adequate.

framework: EU AI Act - GPAI Code of Practice (Safety and Security chapter)
requirement_paraphrase: Signatories obtain assurance that security mitigations meet the Security Goal through independent external security reviews where internal expertise is inadequate, frequent red-teaming of network and physical access management, competitive bug bounties for public-facing endpoints, periodic personnel integrity testing, third-party security reporting channels, endpoint/intrusion detection tools and a security incident response team.
what_is_tested: Security assurance testing of model and infrastructure
who_tests: Signatory provider; independent external security reviewers
interpretation_note: Supports Art 55(1)(d) cybersecurity obligation. Measure 7.4 asks for external security review reports in the Model Report where available.

framework: EU AI Act - GPAI Code of Practice (Safety and Security chapter)
requirement_paraphrase: Signatories run a full systemic risk assessment and mitigation process at least before placing a model on the market, and give the AI Office unredacted access to the Model Report (evaluation results, mitigations, reasons for proceeding) by the time the model is placed on the market; updates within five business days; delay of up to 15 business days only in good faith with an interim report.
what_is_tested: Pre-market reporting of evaluation results to the regulator
interpretation_note: Closest the Code comes to a pre-market filing gate; voluntary code assessed adequate for Art 55. Redactions only where national security law requires.

framework: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/2274 on harmonised standards for high-risk AI systems
requirement_paraphrase: The Commission publishes in the Official Journal the reference of EN 18286:2026 'Artificial intelligence - Quality management system for EU AI Act regulatory purposes', developed under standardisation request C(2025) 3871 (point 9 of Annex I, QMS incl. post-market monitoring); conformity with it gives a presumption of conformity with the requirements it covers from publication; the decision enters into force on publication (OJ 14.10.2026).
what_is_tested: Quality management system (incl. verification, test and validation procedures): presumption of conformity
who_tests: Providers apply; notified bodies and authorities rely on presumption
interpretation_note: Applying the standard is voluntary; it gives a presumption of conformity under AI Act Art 40(1) for the requirements it covers (Art 17 QMS per the JTC 21 feed; the Decision does not name the Article). First and only AI Act harmonised standard cited in the OJ as of 2026-10-16. Standard text is sold by national bodies and was not read.
conflict_flag: yes: supersedes EU-Standards-002 'no OJEU reference yet'
